alignments.note: Finite verb; explicit subject noun stands separately (rule 17).
Proper name; English fronts the subject, reordered under rule 25.

Imperfect recast with a jussive frame: *let ... come to pass* belongs whole to the verb, discontinuous around the subject phrase (rules 17, 25), headed on the lexical verb *come* (rule 24). The margin's *Now when thy words come to pass* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
Construct noun takes its own word.
Finite verb with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical predicate (rule 24).
Construct noun with a supplied *the*: the ASV writes a *the* before each noun, so the rectum's article takes the one before its own word and the construct takes the supplied one (rule 29).
Article on the rectum takes the written *the* standing before its own word; nothing is fronted (rule 29).
*how* answers to no morpheme in the clause; the ASV italicizes it, which corroborates without deciding (rules 7, 30).

The nominal `מַעֲשֵׂהוּ` is recast as a finite clause; the supplied subject and auxiliary belong to that noun's own recasting and are not `added` (rule 46), headed on the verb carrying the lexeme (rule 31).

The suffix is the rectum of the recast construct, and the ASV states that relation with *unto*, which belongs to the rectum's unit (rule 19), headed on the pronoun (rule 24). The competing reading gives *unto* to the recast verb's valency under rule 44; the construct relation is the nearer licenser here.

review_notes: ASV marginal alternative (*Now when thy words come to pass, what etc.*) read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text is what is aligned.
The phrase `מִשְׁפַּט הַנַּעַר` writes a *the* before each English noun, so rule 29's arthrous count governs rather than its fronting case.
